message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements. Below is a comprehensive overview of its key characteristics: | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Standard atomic weight** | 1.008 u (average of isotopes) | | **Isotopes** |
  • ¹H (protium) – 99.98 % natural abundance, one proton, no neutrons.
  • ²H (deuterium) – 0.02 % natural abundance, one proton + one neutron.
  • ³H (tritium) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr, one proton + two neutrons.
| | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative because H tends to lose an electron rather than gain one). | | **Boiling point (STP)** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | | **Melting point (STP)** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density (at STP)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) | | **Molar volume (ideal gas, 273 K, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | | **Heat capacity (Cp)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) | | **Thermal conductivity** | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) | | **Electrical conductivity** | Very low as a neutral gas; becomes highly conductive when ionized (plasma). | | **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, oxidizes to water or oxides. | | **Bonding behavior** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂), ionic bonds (as H⁺ or H⁻), and participates in hydrogen bonding (in water, alcohols, etc.). | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR); characteristic emission/absorption lines used in astrophysics. | | **Nuclear spin** | Protium (¹H): I = ½; Deuterium (²H): I = 1; Tritium (³H): I = ½. | | **Magnetic moment** | 2.792847 µB (proton magnetic moment). | | **Abundance** | ~75 % by mass in the universe; ~90 % of all atoms in the cosmos. | ### Physical Properties | Category | Details | |----------|---------| | **State at room temperature** | Diatomic gas (H₂). | | **Solubility in water** | Slightly soluble (~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C). | | **Flammability** | Highly flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % in air. | | **Color & odor** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless. | | **Pressure dependence** | At 1 atm, H₂ remains gaseous until ~14 K; above this, it condenses into liquid or solid phases. | ### Chemical Properties | Reaction Type | Typical Behavior | |---------------|------------------| | **Oxidation** | Combustion produces water vapor: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O. | | **Halogenation** | Reacts with Cl₂, Br₂, I₂ to form HX (hydrohalic acids). | | **Acid–base** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H₃O⁺) or base (forming H⁻ in metal hydrides). | | **Redox** | Can act as reducing agent (e.g., in the production of ammonia via Haber process). | | **Catalysis** | Used as a catalyst in hydrogenation reactions; also involved in catalytic converters. | ### Nuclear Properties | Feature | Notes | |---------|-------| | **Proton** | Fundamental particle; defines hydrogen’s identity. | | **Neutron count** | Determines isotope; influences nuclear stability and reaction pathways. | | **Half‑life of tritium** | 12.32 years; decays via β⁻ emission to helium‑3. | | **Applications** | Tritium used in self‑lighting devices, fusion research, radiolabeling. | --- #### Quick Reference Table (Standard Conditions) | Property | Symbol | Value | |----------|--------|-------| | Atomic number | Z | 1 | | Mass | m | 1.00794 u | | Density | ρ | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | | Boiling point | T_b | –252.87 °C | | Melting point | T_m | –259.16 °C | | Ionization energy | IE₁ | 13.598 eV | | Electron affinity | EA | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ | | Electronegativity | χ | 2.20 | | Heat capacity | Cp | 28.84 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | These properties collectively define hydrogen’s role in chemistry, physics, biology, and cosmology—from fueling stars to enabling life on Earth.
